title: Dispatch BBA 8: Alderwick Bell Rings One Final Time
summary: Two books record the discharge of a child who escaped the hospital fire.
author: Clara Vale, Staff Correspondent
paragraphs: At 5:40 this morning, Miss Morrow entered Elsie Gray's name and the date of her release beside Patient 42 in the admission register. She then wrote the same entry in the discharge ledger. Sister Kells watched without speaking.

Mrs. Arden placed her grandmother's brass clapper in the hand of a porter who appeared beside Sister Kells. The porter was Joseph Fenner, the market worker who had first reported the bell. He said he did not know why he was there. The clapper fit the bell inside the ward.

The hospital doors closed. The upper window and the staircase faded from view. On the ward's intake slate, all sixty-three living names remained visible for a moment, then dissolved into the surface of the stone. The bell did not sound again.

Sister Kells remained visible for a few seconds after the doors were gone. She held up the ledger so Miss Morrow could see the forty-second entry. Then the doorway became ordinary wall and the sound of the market returned.

The council reopened the square at noon. The Institute has retained its recording and the municipal archive has placed the original register under sealed preservation. Miss Morrow says she will not return to the square without reason.
